name: Picture-in-Picture and automatic PiP
plain: Pops a video into a small floating window above other apps.
meaning: Floats a video over other apps; with camera access, auto PiP can keep a video call visible when the person switches tabs. Chrome gives a separate prompt for camera-based auto PiP.

access.prompt_ui: Manual PiP needs a click; Chrome 134+ auto PiP for video call sites is gated by the camera or microphone grant and engagement.
access.revocation: Close the PiP window; Site settings > Automatic picture-in-picture

firefox.v: Video PiP not supported in Firefox as a web API; browser built-in toggle only

limits.headline: Can float a video in a small window over your other apps
limits.user_action: You click the picture in picture button on a video, or switch tabs during a call
can: Pop a video into a small floating window that stays on top
Keep a video call visible when you switch tabs, if you allowed camera access
Let you move and resize the window
cannot: Float a video without your click, except automatic mode for video call sites in Chrome 134 and later
Show anything except the video itself
Take over the screen or see other windows
Work in Firefox or on most phone browsers
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, Safari and Samsung Internet support it on desktop. Firefox and iPhone browsers do not.

story.what_it_is: Pops a video out into a small floating window that stays above other apps.

marketing.name: Automatic picture in picture
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes automatic PiP, so a video call keeps showing in a floating window when you switch tabs.

marketing.name: Picture in Picture API
marketing.pitch: Developer docs describe how a page can float a video in a small window above other windows.

story.for_you: You click a button or tab away, and the video shrinks into a floating window in the corner. You can keep watching a lecture or a call while you work in another tab. It often moves and resizes.
story.for_makers: A floating window keeps people in a call or a video while they multitask, which raises time spent and cuts dropped calls. For calls, Chrome gives a separate prompt before auto PiP can start with the camera on. Makers also use it to keep the logo and controls visible.

use_cases.example: You are in a Google Meet call, switch to a spreadsheet to find a number, and the call shrinks into a floating window so you do not miss anyone.
You watch a YouTube video, switch to your email, and the video floats on top so you can keep following along.
You stream a cloud game or a Twitch match in a floating window while you check your guide or chat in another tab.
A live sports or news stream floats over your work during a big match or a breaking event.
A recorded lecture floats beside your notes while you type, and you pause it with one click.
A Document PiP window floats a timer or sticky notes over your other work while you stay in the flow.

risks: Floating window can hide something important
Auto PiP can show your camera feed while you switch tabs

technical_bounds: Needs a gesture for manual PiP

abuse: Keeping an ad or call overlay visible

history.change: Automatic PiP for video conferencing sites
